We integrate Reading Order into the Recognition stage, with both tasks handled by the same model. This design improves both speed and accuracy.\n\nWe also designed the system this way to make customization easier. We have found that Layout Analysis varies more across document domains than any other module, and it is typically the part that document parsing providers need to customize most. Existing document parsing tools either assign it to the Recognition model or use a dedicated model that also handles Reading Order. OXR's design achieves the simplest access method for Layout Analysis, and any Layout Analysis model can work well with the OXR model.\n\n![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoMarkAI/image_bed/main/OXR_README/assets/oxr_pipeline.png)\n\n\n\n### Improvement Through the RSI Loop\n\nFor a task like document parsing, where ground-truth answers exist, we have long wanted an engineering system that helps the core model improve itself. The diagram below shows OXR's RSI approach. It targets samples the model gets wrong or handles weakly, improving performance without human annotation. This has made our iteration faster than ever.\n\n![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SoMarkAI/image_bed/main/OXR_README/assets/oxr_rsi_loop.png)\n\n\n\n## Quick Start\n\n<a id=\"free-api\"></a>\n\n### 0. 🔥 🆓 Free API\n\nOXR provides a free API so you can test parsing on your own documents without registering or requesting an API key.\n\nWe'll keep the free API online until we can no longer afford to run it.\n\n⚠️ Note: We do not recommend using the Free OXR API in production. We do not guarantee service stability, and requests are queued, so processing speed may vary slightly.\n\n| Online Demo | https://free-oxr.somark.ai | https://free-oxr.somark.cn |\n|-|-|-|\n| API URL | https://free-oxr.somark.ai/api/v1 | https://free-oxr.somark.cn/api/v1 |\n| API documentation | [https://docs.somark.ai/api-reference](https://docs.somark.ai/api-reference) | https://docs.somark.cn/api-reference |\n\n> somark.cn is a mirror of somark.ai. Choose the domain that works best for your region.\n\nOXR's document parsing API is compatible with SoMark's official document parsing API. You can use SoMark's official document parsing CLI tools, somark-py and somark-js, by changing the **Base URL**. See Section 1.4 for supported endpoints and output formats.\n\n```Bash\n# using python\npip install somark\n# or using js\nnpm install -g somark-js\n\nsomark --base-url https://free-oxr.somark.ai/api/v1 --api-key dummy \\\n  parse document.pdf --formats md,json --out ./parsed-output/\n```\n\n\n\n### 1. Run Locally\n\n```Plain Text\nOperating system: Linux\nGPU: NVIDIA (with BF16 support)\nDriver: NVIDIA driver (compatible with CUDA 13.0)\nPython: 3.12 (for model downloads / running from source)\nGPU memory to get started: 24GB on a single GPU (for low-concurrency testing)\nRecommended GPU memory: ≥48GB on a single GPU (for long documents / higher concurrency)\n```\n\n#### 1.1 Download the Code and Models\n\n| Model | Download links | Precision | Includes a lightweight layout analysis model? |\n|-|-|-|-|\n| OXR-1.0 | [🤗 Hugging Face ](https://huggingface.co/SoMarkAI/OXR-1.0)  <br/>[🤖 ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/SoMark/OXR-1.0) | BF16 | Yes, in the layout_analysis folder |\n\nFirst, get the code and prepare the environment for downloading the models:\n\n```Bash\ngit clone https://github.com/SoMarkAI/OXR.git\ncd OXR\n\n# pip install -U huggingface_hub\nhf download SoMarkAI/OXR-1.0 --local-dir ./models/OXR-1.0\n\n# or using ModelScope\n# pip install -U modelscope-hub\nmodelscope download SoMark/OXR-1.0 --local_dir ./models/OXR-1.0\n```\n\n#### 1.2 Start the Services\n\n##### 1.2.1 Run with Docker (Recommended)\n\nWe recommend Docker to configure and start all services together.\n\n```Bash\ndocker build -f docker/Dockerfile.allinone -t oxr-1.0 .\ndocker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host \\\n  -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \\\n  -v \"$PWD/models/OXR-1.0:/models/oxr-model:ro\" \\\n  oxr-1.0\n```\n\nOnce the startup logs show that the services are ready, open http://localhost:8000/demo or http://localhost:8000/docs.\nThe first startup may take longer. The default startup timeout is 900 seconds.\nSee How to use OXR for more advanced options and usage examples.\n\n\n##### 1.2.2 Run from Source\n\nAfter downloading the code and models, start the following three services separately. Each service uses its own process and virtual environment. Run all commands from the OXR repository root. The document parsing API depends on both the OXR model service and the Layout Analysis model service, so start the two model APIs first.\n\n**OXR Model Service (Port 8080)**\n\nOXR supports vLLM, but the official vLLM release does not yet support OXR inference. We provide an out-of-tree plugin and a loading script in the model weights folder on Hugging Face. No recompilation is needed: you can use the plugin directly with the official vLLM Docker image or CLI.\n\n```Bash\n# pip install vllm==0.25.1 transformers==5.13.1\n\nMODEL_PATH=\"$PWD/models/OXR-1.0\" \\\n  bash services/oxr/start_vllm.sh \\\n  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 --max-num-seqs 16\n```\n\n**Layout Analysis Model Service (Port 8081)**\n\nThe Layout Analysis model weights are included in the OXR model weights folder downloaded earlier.\n\n```Bash\n# pip install torch==2.11.0 torchvision==0.26.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130\n# pip install -r services/layout_analyze/requirements.txt\n\nMODEL_PATH=\"$PWD/models/OXR-1.0/layout_analysis/last.pth\" \\\nDFINE_DEVICE=cuda \\\n  python -m uvicorn dfine_la.api... [L2]   "content": "# Filmimic\n\n**Real-time film emulation for Unreal Engine. Drop in an Actor, pick a look, then make it yours.**\n\n[中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) · [Full user guide / 完整使用指南](docs/guide.zh-CN.md) · [Build and validation](docs/validation.md) · [License scope](docs/third-party-notices.md)\n\n![ArchVis interior rendered in Unreal Engine with Filmimic Kodak Portra 400](docs/images/portra.png)\n\nFilmimic brings film color, animated grain, halation, bloom, lens artifacts and framing controls into one Unreal post-process workflow. It includes **21 looks**, **197 effect parameters**, reusable preset assets, Blueprint controls and four quality tiers.\n\nThe initial public source snapshot is **1.0.0**. The tested baseline is **Unreal Engine 5.8.3 / Windows / DX12 / SM6**. This repository contains plugin sources and the assets needed by those sources; it does not contain Unreal Engine, compiled plugin binaries, private project maps or build caches.\n\n## See the difference\n\nSame scene, camera and lighting; different preset selections. These are actual Unreal `SceneCapture2D` renders, not externally applied filters or generated concept art.\n\n| Native Unreal | Kodak Portra 400 |\n| :---: | :---: |\n| ![Native Unreal output](docs/images/native.png) | ![Kodak Portra 400 preset](docs/images/portra.png) |\n\n| Kodak Gold 200 | Red Velvet | Cinematica |\n| :---: | :---: | :---: |\n| ![Kodak Gold 200 preset](docs/images/gold.png) | ![Red Velvet preset](docs/images/velvet.png) | ![Cinematica preset](docs/images/cinematica.png) |\n\nThe showcase uses the project's **ArchVis sample interior**, with its original lights, Lumen GI/reflections and temporal anti-aliasing requested. Each 2560×1440 image is captured after 100 real Editor warm-up frames. [Capture settings and reproduction instructions](docs/screenshots.md) document the camera and required sample content. The map and its assets are not bundled with the plugin. Preset names identify artistic looks, not a guarantee of a physical film stock's response or an endorsement by a film manufacturer.\n\n## What you can control\n\n| Area | Included controls |\n| --- | --- |\n| Film emulation | 14 film branches plus None, white balance, highlight/shadow tone, saturation, clarity and sharpness |\n| Grain | Quick size/roughness choices or advanced ISO, size, roughness and softness; optional animation |\n| Lens effects | Vignette, bloom, glints, halation, soft glow, ghosts, flare streaks, dispersion, fringing and lens dirt |\n| Grading | Flicker, split toning, punchiness, color adjustments and stylized 2D blur |\n| Overlays | Composition grids, borders, film sprockets and text watermarks |\n| Workflow | Shared or per-Actor settings, parameter resets, name-based Blueprint access and save-your-own presets |\n\nParameters are grouped in Details. Controls that do not affect the current branch are greyed out. Hover a label for a Chinese explanation, units and its parameter identifier; angle controls display degrees.\n\n## Install from source\n\n1. Install UE 5.8.3 and the C++ toolchain supported by that engine version.\n2. With your Editor closed, clone the repository into your project's plugin folder:\n\n   ```powershell\n   git clone https://github.com/DreamyLab30/Filmimic.git .\\Plugins\\Filmimic\n   ```\n\n3. Build your project's **Editor** target. A Blueprint-only project may need a C++ module or a locally built plugin package before it can load a source plugin.\n4. Open the project, enable **Filmimic** under **Edit → Plugins**, then restart the Editor. The shader module loads at engine startup.\n5. Add **FilmimicActor** to your level. In Details, choose **Preset**. Enable **Show Plugin Content** in the Content Browser to browse `/Filmimic` assets.\n\nTo build a distributable plugin locally, use the supplied wrapper with your own engine location and a **new output directory outside the repository**:\n\n```powershell\n.\\scripts\\build.ps1 -EngineRoot $env:UE_ROOT -OutputDirectory $env:FILMIMIC_PACKAGE_DIR\n```\n\n`UE_ROOT` is the folder containing the engine's `Engine` directory. BuildPlugin compiling successfully does not verify a cooked game; that is a separate test.\n\n## Make a look in five steps\n\n1. Select a preset such as **Kodak Portra 400**, **Cinematica** or **Red Velvet**.\n2. Click **Edit on this actor** to copy the shared preset into this Actor's local settings.\n3. Adjust exposure and film color first, then grain and lens effects. Use the group checkboxes to isolate an effect.\n4. Enter a name in **Save as Preset**, then click **Save Preset**. It writes a new asset under `/Game/FilmimicPresets`, selects it immediately and adds it to the preset dropdown. Existing names require overwrite confirmation.\n5. Save the level to retain the Actor's reference to the new preset.\n\n**Shared settings** follow the preset asset, including later edits to it. **Local settings** affect just this Actor. Selecting another preset in local mode replaces the local values; save a useful look before switching. Presets store effect settings and resource bindings, not an Actor's position, area radius or `Weight`.\n\n## The three controls worth learning first\n\n| Control | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Enabled** | Off restores the native UE path for this Actor. |\n| **Weight** | Blend between native Unreal output (`0`) and Filmimic (`1`). Use this for fades and before/after comparisons. |\n| **Intensity** | Strength inside the Filmimic effect chain. At `0`, the AgX display transform remains; this is different from disabling Filmimic. |\n\n**Use Engine Exposure** is on by default. **Exposure EV** adds stops before the effect chain. The quick **Cinematic** quality tier is the default; **Reference** retains the highest-precision path and is much more expensive.\n\n## Blueprints, Sequencer and regions\n\nGet the Actor's `Filmimic` component and call:\n\n```text\nSetMenuParameterByName(\n    Name = \"Film Emulation / Film Type / Film Type\",\n    Option = \"VELVET / Vivid\")\n\nSetParameterByName(\n    Name = \"Lens Effects / Halation / Strength\",\n    Value = 0.2)\n\nFadeWeight(TargetWeight = 0, DurationSeconds = 1.5)\nBlendToPreset(TargetPreset, DurationSeconds = 2.0)\n```\n\n`GetAnimatableParameterNames` lists valid names; `GetParameterDescription` returns their explanations. `ApplyPreset` follows a shared asset; `LoadPresetAsLocal` copies it into this Actor. Transitions interpolate continuous controls; menu and switch choices change at the midpoint.\n\nThe **Animated Controls A–D** slots expose four selected numeric parameters to Sequencer. `Weight`, `Intensity` and `Exposure EV` also support keyframes. Clear a slot to stop its value overriding the ordinary parameter.\n\nLeave **Unbound** on for a world-wide look. Turn it off to use **Radius** and **Blend Distance** around the Actor. The highest-priority enabled candidate owns the view and fades toward native Unreal output; overlapping Filmimic Actors do not perform arbitrary multi-look blending.\n\n## Built-in looks\n\nDefault · Astra 1996 · Cinematica · Eternally Expired · Golden Chrome · Kodak 1971 · Kodak Ektra · Kodak Gold 200 · Kodak Portra 160 · Kodak Portra 400 · Kodak Portra Pro · Nostalgic Breeze · Pacifica · Red Velvet · SoCal · Sprint Clarity · Stonewall · Summer of 76 · Superia · Victoria · Yeast Lords\n\n`FilmimicActor.GetAvailablePresets()` returns these 21 assets. `FilmimicPresetCatalog.FindPresetByName()` resolves a display name. Saved user presets appear after the bundled looks in the editor dropdown.\n\n## Performance and support boundaries\n\nHistorical development measurements on an RTX 4090, Default preset, isolated SceneCapture and Insights GPU timing:\n\n| Output | Cinematic | Balanced | Performance | Reference |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| 1920×1080 | 1.98 ms | 1.85 ms | 1.65 ms | 28.7 ms |\n| 3840×2160 | 9.8 ms | — | 3.5 ms | — |\n\nThese are plugin GPU timings from the development harness, not complete game-frame times or a fresh cross-hardware benchmark. At high resolution, Performance reduces the grain domain and may soften/ring high-contrast edges. Profile your own scene with `stat gpu`. [Validation notes](docs/validation.md) distinguish historical evidence from this repository's fresh checks.\n\n- Editor viewport and PIE were exercised during development. The standalone source build and the ArchVis captures were verified for this public snapshot.\n- Cooked-game execution, other engine versions/platforms and Movie Render Queue are not yet verified.\n- HDR output encoding has numerical checks; a physical HDR display has not been validated. VR is experimental and disabled by default.\n- SceneCapture participation is opt-in via **Allow Scene Capture**. Reflection and planar-reflection captures are excluded.\n- At `Weight = 1`, Filmimic replaces the tonemapper. UE tonemapper color grading/LUTs therefore do not compose as ordinary additional grading; use Filmimic controls or native-image blending deliberately.\n- The plugin's **Stylized 2D Blur** is a whole-image effect. It does not replace velocity-based motion blur.\n\n## Contribute and report problems\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the workflow and [SECURITY](SECURITY.md) for private vulnerability reporting. A useful rendering issue includes engine/RHI, resolution, preset, quality tier and an isolated reproduction.\n\n## License\n\n**GPL-2.0-or-later**, with third-party notices and the Blinker font's separate OFL terms. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [license scope](docs/third-party-notices.md). Unreal Engine is licensed separately; this repository grants no exception to Epic's terms. The code is publicly inspectable, and downstream distribution must respect the applicable component licenses and permissions.\n",

Exact reproduction with the released package is not guaranteed.\n\n## System overview\n\nPika H3 Flex is one video-and-audio model family with two task adapters: FL2VA for text and endpoint-frame conditioning, and Ref2VA for multimodal references. It builds on [MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3) and generates video with synchronized stereo audio in six sampling steps.\n\nThe inference pipeline encodes the prompt and input media, generates video and audio latents with the selected Pika H3 Flex adapter, then decodes and combines them into an MP4. The package downloads the pinned base components and adapter automatically. Use the [prompt guide](docs/prompt-guidance.md) to describe scenes, motion, dialogue, ambience and music; optional [prompt enhancement](https://dev.pika.art/models/pika/pika-h3-flex/prompt-rewriter) is available through the Pika API.\n\n### Input and output specifications\n\n| Category                 | Specification                                                                                                     |\n| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Input modalities         | Text; first/last images; image, video and audio references, depending on the selected mode                        |\n| Native output resolution | 480p / 768p across all 11 supported aspect ratios; exact pixel dimensions follow the selected aspect-ratio bucket |\n| Output duration          | Requested integer durations of 5–15 seconds; actual length follows the model frame grid                          |\n| Output aspect ratios     | 21:9, 16:9, 3:2, 4:3, 5:4, 1:1, 4:5, 3:4, 2:3, 9:16, 9:21; dimensions use the packaged resolution buckets         |\n| Output frame rate        | 24 fps                                                                                                            |\n| Output audio             | 32 kHz stereo, mixed into the generated video                                                                     |\n| Output files             | MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio, plus JSON generation metadata                                                 |\n| Prompt input             | Text or a UTF-8 prompt file; 1–8,000 characters                                                                  |\n| Sampling                 | Six generator evaluations using the released adapter's sampling schedule                                          |\n\nDurations are rounded up to the supported frame grid: a 5-second request produces 124 frames (about 5.17 seconds), and a 15-second request produces 362 frames (about 15.08 seconds). Native resolution and aspect ratio jointly determine the actual canvas dimensions.\n\n### Generation modes and reference limits\n\n| Mode                              | Inputs                                                                      | Adapter / CLI task  |\n| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |\n| Text to video and audio           | Prompt, without input media                                                 | FL2VA / `t2va`    |\n| First-frame conditioning          | Prompt and one opening frame                                                | FL2VA / `i2va`    |\n| Last-frame conditioning           | Prompt and one ending frame                                                 | FL2VA / `l2va`    |\n| First-and-last-frame conditioning | Prompt and both endpoint frames                                             | FL2VA / `fl2va`   |\n| Multimodal references             | Prompt and ordered image/video references, optionally with audio references | Ref2VA / `ref2va` |\n\nRef2VA accepts up to **9 images, 3 videos and 3 standalone audio clips**, with **12 reference files total**. At least one image or video is required. Each video or standalone audio clip must be **2–15 seconds**; combined video duration and combined standalone-audio duration must each be at most **15 seconds**. A video's embedded soundtrack stays with that video and does not count as an additional standalone audio file.\n\nThese are accepted input limits, not a guarantee that every maximum-size combination fits GPU memory. The package runs one request on one GPU, with optional CPU offload. See [hardware requirements and tested configurations](docs/hardware.md) for representative H100 results and memory guidance.\n\n## Pika API extensions\n\nExtend your generation workflow with Pika’s hosted endpoints:\n\n| Feature                 | Support                                            | Endpoint                                                                           |\n| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Higher-resolution video | Generate 1080p, 2K and 4K video from a draft video | [Draft to video](https://dev.pika.art/models/pika/pika-h3-flex/draft-to-video)      |\n| Audio stems             | Obtain separate audio stems                        | [Audio stems](https://dev.pika.art/models/pika/pika-h3-flex/audio-stems)            |\n| Prompt enhancement      | Enhance generation prompts                         | [Prompt enhancement](https://dev.pika.art/models/pika/pika-h3-flex/prompt-rewriter) |\n\nThese optional hosted services are separate from the downloadable adapters and local inference package. The specifications above describe local model inference; see each endpoint’s documentation for its API capabilities and usage.\n\n## Install\n\nThe command and Python distribution are named `pika-h3-pro`.\n\nClone the repository, then enter its directory:\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex.git\ncd Pika-H3-Flex\n```\n\nFor pip installation, install system `git`, `patch`, `ffmpeg` and a C compiler with development headers first (for example, `build-essential` on Debian/Ubuntu). Triton needs the compiler at runtime. Docker and Conda recipes supply these prerequisites.\n\nUse Python 3.12, an NVIDIA GPU and a compatible driver. Representative cases are tested on one H100 80GB per request; H200 and B300 remain untested. Longer clips and large reference sets can exceed GPU memory. Downloading both tasks acquired approximately 210 GB of base files plus 5.5 GB of adapters; allow additional space for dependencies and download staging. See [tested cases and memory measurements](docs/hardware.md).\n\n**GPU selection:** the current package runs one request on one GPU. The examples expose a single GPU with `--gpus 'device=0'`; exposing eight GPUs does not shard or accelerate a request. Multiple idle GPUs can run independent processes. Start qualification at 480p / 5 seconds. Multi-GPU inference within one request is not implemented in this package.\n\n```bash\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\npython tools/apply_diffusers_patches.py\npython -m pip install --no-deps -e .\npika-h3-pro --help\n```\n\nAlternatively, create the Conda environment, then install the package:\n\n```bash\nconda env create -f environment.yml\nconda activate pika-h3-pro\npython tools/apply_diffusers_patches.py\npython -m pip install --no-deps -e .\n```\n\nFor Docker:\n\n```bash\ndocker build -t pika-h3-pro .\ndocker run --rm --gpus 'device=0' pika-h3-pro --help\n```\n\nThe three recipes share `requirements.txt`. Authentication, when required, is passed at runtime using `HF_TOKEN` or the Hugging Face cache; never put tokens into image layers.\n\n## Generate\n\nThe released adapter pair and immutable HF pin are recorded in [release.json](release.json). Use the pinned release with:\n\n```bash\nexport MODEL_REPO=Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex\nexport MODEL_REVISION=0ddf55ad7067ca1e76812253bd7b4600df87f759\n```\n\n```bash\npika-h3-pro --task t2va --prompt-file examples/prompts/t2va.txt \\\n  --model-repo \"$MODEL_REPO\" --revision \"$MODEL_REVISION\" \\\n  --resolution 480p --aspect 16:9 --duration 5 --seed 42 --output outputs/sample.mp4\n```\n\nUse `--task i2va --first-image first.png`, `--task l2va --last-image last.png`, or `--task fl2va --first-image first.png --last-image last.png` for endpoint conditioning. Ref2VA accepts ordered `--ref image:subject.png` inputs with a reference prompt:\n\n```bash\npika-h3-pro --task ref2va --prompt-file examples/prompts/ref2va.txt \\\n  --ref image:subject.png --model-repo \"$MODEL_REPO\" --revision \"$MODEL_REVISION\" \\\n  --resolution 480p --duration 5 --output outputs/reference.mp4\n```\n\nThe downloader acquires the selected adapter and its pinned MiniMax-H3 components. Local snapshot overrides exist for validation, but are not required by the public workflow. The package validates adapter hashes and sampling parameters before loading the transformer. Adapter files remain FP32; resident LoRA computation uses BF16, preserving native mixed-precision model boundaries.\n\nSee [prompt guidance](docs/prompt-guidance.md). Prompt files are read verbatim; no prompt rewriting service is required. The output JSON records the final prompt, seed, artifact identity, geometry, offload setting and timings. Do not publish a metadata file containing a private prompt without reviewing it.\n\nFor requests that exceed GPU memory, add `--cpu-offload`. This keeps transformer weights on the CPU and prefetches blocks to the GPU; it trades substantial host RAM and additional transfer time for lower sampling VRAM. It does not offload the text encoder or VAEs, so the reduced sampling peak is not a minimum GPU requirement. The default keeps the transformer on the GPU. Consult the verification table before choosing clip length and resolution.\n\nFor example, this 768p/15s configuration passed on a single H100 80GB with offload:\n\n```bash\npika-h3-pro --model-repo \"$MODEL_REPO\" --revision \"$MODEL_REVISION\" \\\n  --task t2va --prompt-file examples/prompts/t2va.txt --resolution 768p \\\n  --duration 15 --seed 42 --cpu-offload --output outputs/long-768p.mp4\n```\n\nRequested durations are 5–15 integer seconds. The model uses a 17n+5 frame grid at 24fps, so actual duration differs slightly from the request. The [verification table](docs/hardware.md) records tested cases; it does not qualify every aspect/duration/reference combination. Raw video and audio references use `--ref video:clip.mp4` and `--ref audio:sound.wav`. Video soundtracks are included automatically. Limits: 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audio references, 12 references total. Each video/audio source must be 2–15 seconds; video durations and standalone audio durations separately sum to at most 15 seconds. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and others.\n\n**Play the 31 games:** [fal-video-to-game.vercel.app](https://fal-video-to-game.vercel.app)\n\n![Video to Game: the generated video shrinks, the code and the fal assets come in, the game appears](gallery/hero.gif)\n\n31 original games, every one rebuilt from a 10 to 15 s video generated with MiniMax H3 Max on fal: 1,013 fal calls\n(594 images, 194 3D models, 290 sounds and music tracks), 202 USD in total, about 6 USD per game. Every game is a\nsingle `index.html` with Three.js and nothing else: no engine, no template, no other library.\n\n## Why\n\nAgents cannot design a game's look. Asked for \"a game where a boy glides between flying whales\", they ship grey\nboxes, a default sky and a camera that fights the player. A video model is good at exactly that part, so let it go\nfirst, and make the agent match it:\n\n- **The video is the design document.** `study_video.py` turns it into frames, a contact sheet, a palette and\n  cut times; the agent writes a spec (camera, hero, the one mechanic, the key moment, the look) from named frames.\n- **Every asset comes from fal, from the video's own frames.** Concept sheets with Nano Banana Pro, clean cutouts,\n  image to 3D (Meshy, Tripo, Hunyuan 3D), rigging and animations, sound effects and music, all logged with\n  `fal_asset.py`. Nothing drawn by hand, nothing downloaded.\n- **The look is a spec, not polish.** Tone mapping, one grade, fog, bloom, vignette and grain from the first scene,\n  and a side-by-side picture of the video and the game at the same three spots after every change.\n- **Calm the world so the game reads.** One harmonized palette, dense but grouped, the hero and everything you can\n  interact with standing out on a quiet background. No text on screen.\n- **The agent plays its own game.** A keyboard scenario reads `window.__game` like a player reads the screen,\n  `record_play.mjs` films it at the real frame rate, `best_window.py` finds the liveliest seconds. probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask \"what happens when someone checks out?\" or \"what breaks if I change this?\" and the honest answer is *no idea*.\n\nFloorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work.\n\n- **For builders:** understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code.\n- **For teams:** onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file.\n- **For working with AI:** after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why.\n\n## Features\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"50%\" valign=\"top\">\n\n**🗺️ A map at every zoom**<br>\nStart with the whole app, then double-click into a part, a group of files, a file, and its endpoints. Each view shows what it's used by and what it uses.\n\n</td>\n<td width=\"50%\" valign=\"top\">\n\n**💬 Plain English everywhere**<br>\n\"Takes card payments at checkout\", not \"Stripe API wrapper\". Technical terms are explained on hover, and one switch shows the developer view.\n\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**🔌 Real connections, across repos**<br>\nIt follows imports, and matches each web request in your frontend to the server endpoint that answers it, even across separate repos.\n\n</td>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**🖥️ Start from a screen**<br>\nPick a page you know and see everything behind it: its parts, the requests it makes, the server code, the data, and outside services.\n\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**🧭 Ask the map**<br>\n\"How does a refund reach the customer's card?\" comes back as an answer plus a mini-map of just the pieces involved, with a step-by-step walkthrough.\n\n</td>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**🩺 Health check**<br>\nFinds passwords in code, endpoints anyone can use without signing in, unused files and files too big to edit safely. Each comes with a ready-to-paste fix.\n\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**🟢 Recent work**<br>\nThe cards your AI just changed light up green, each with a note on how the change serves what you asked for.\n\n</td>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n\n**⚡ Stays current, stays yours**<br>\nUpdates re-read only what changed, and an open map reloads itself. Everything runs on your machine, and nothing is committed to git.\n\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\nPlus guided **flows** you can request in plain words, a one-minute **Start here** tour, search, keyboard shortcuts, and right-click actions on every card.\n\n### Also: blueprints, for apps you haven't built yet\n\nFloorplan is made for mapping code you already have. It can also start from a PRD, a spec or a description of something you want to build, and draw a **blueprint**: the same kind of map, showing every part, file, endpoint and screen you'd need and how they'd fit together. Cards are dashed to show it's a plan. Instead of a Health check you get a review of what the plan still leaves open, each part has a ready request to build it, and you can reshape the plan from the map (\"also plan out refunds\"). Once the code exists, the blueprint becomes a map of the real thing. See [Plan something you haven't built yet](docs/getting-started.md#plan-something-you-havent-built-yet).\n\n## See it in action\n\nWant to click around yourself? Open the [live demo](https://haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo/): the real Brewline map beside a scripted conversation, in Claude Code or Codex.\n\n<table>\n<tr>\n<td width=\"50%\" valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/ask.png\" alt=\"An answer board: the gift subscription traced from the gift page to the friend's inbox, with numbered cards and a written walkthrough\">\n<p><b>Ask the map.</b> A real answer, from the Claude Code CLI in 31 seconds. It traced the gift from form to inbox across two repos, and spotted two bugs along the way.</p>\n</td>\n<td width=\"50%\" valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/screens.png\" alt=\"Everything behind the Gift page: its form, the requests it makes, the server code, the database, Stripe and SendGrid\">\n<p><b>Start from a screen.</b> Pick any page and see everything behind it, from the button down to the database and outside services.</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/recent.png\" alt=\"The Recent work board for a gift subscriptions feature: what was asked, what was done, and a note on every changed card\">\n<p><b>Recent work.</b> What you asked for, what changed, and why each change was needed, on one board.</p>\n</td>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/health.png\" alt=\"The Health panel listing a secret key written into the code and an endpoint anyone can use, each with Show on map and a Fix button\">\n<p><b>Health check.</b> A password left in the code and an endpoint anyone can call, each with a one-click fix prompt.</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n<tr>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/inside.png\" alt=\"Inside the Business rules part of the server: its files in the middle, what uses them on the left, and outside services on the right\">\n<p><b>Zoom in.</b> Inside any part: what's in it, what uses it, and what it relies on. Green tags mark what just changed.</p>\n</td>\n<td valign=\"top\">\n<img src=\"docs/images/flow.png\" alt=\"A guided flow, step 4 of 6, showing the main server emailing the gift code through SendGrid\">\n<p><b>Guided flows.</b> Watch a request travel through the app step by step, or ask for a new one to be traced.</p>\n</td>\n</tr>\n</table>\n\n## Install\n\nYou need [Node.js 18+](https://nodejs.org) and either Claude Code or Codex. Floorplan runs on the plan you already have, with no API keys.\n\n### Claude Code\n\nIn the desktop app's Code tab or the CLI:\n\n```bash\nclaude plugin marketplace add haydenschmitty/floorplan\nclaude plugin install floorplan@floorplan\n```\n\nStart a new session and it's ready. Installing the Claude Code CLI is recommended even if you use the desktop app, because it lets the map's Ask bar read your real code. More in [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md).\n\n### Codex\n\nSigned in with ChatGPT. No terminal needed:\n\n1. In the Codex app, open **Plugins** and choose **Add a marketplace**.\n2. For **Source**, enter `haydenschmitty/floorplan` and click **Add marketplace**.\n3. Find **Floorplan** and click **+** to install it.\n\nOr, from a terminal:\n\n```bash\ncodex plugin marketplace add haydenschmitty/floorplan\ncodex plugin add floorplan@floorplan\n```\n\nStart a new chat and ask for a floorplan, or type `$floorplan`. The map's Ask bar runs on your own Codex sign-in, with no API key. More in [Floorplan in Codex](docs/codex.md).\n\n## Quick start\n\n1. Open your project in Claude Code or Codex. For a frontend and backend in separate repos, open the folder that holds both.\n2. Ask:\n   > Make me a floorplan of this app.\n\n   (In Codex you can also type `$floorplan`.)\n3. Explore. The map opens on its own, starting with a short tour.\n\nWhen you've done more work, ask:\n\n> Update the floorplan.\n\nOnly what changed is re-read, and what you just worked on lights up under **Recent work**.\n\n**No code yet?** Floorplan can plan an app from a PRD or spec instead. Share the document and ask:\n\n> Here's my PRD. Make me a floorplan of what we'd need to build.\n\nYou get a [blueprint](#also-blueprints-for-apps-you-havent-built-yet) of the planned system, clearly marked as a plan.\n\n### Things to try\n\n| Ask Claude Code or Codex | Ask the map |\n|---|---|\n| \"Make me a floorplan of this app\" | \"What happens when someone places an order?\" |\n| \"Update the floorplan\" | \"Where do we talk to Stripe?\" |\n| \"Fix the important issues from the floorplan's Health check\" | \"If I change the users table, what breaks?\" |\n| \"Add a flow showing how a new user signs up\" | \"Which files handle login?\" |\n| \"Rewrite the floorplan for developers\" | \"What did we change for refunds?\" |\n\n## How it works\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    code[\"Your codebase<br/>one repo or several\"] --> scan[\"Scan<br/>files, imports, routes, requests\"]\n    scan --> agent[\"Claude or Codex<br/>names the parts, describes every file\"]\n    agent --> build[\"Build<br/>map, health, screens, recent work\"]\n    build --> map[\"floorplan/index.html<br/>opens in your browser\"]\n    map -. \"update the floorplan\" .-> scan\n```\n\nScripts do the mechanical work: finding repos, parsing code in a dozen languages, matching web requests to endpoints, laying out the map. They're plain Node with no dependencies. Claude or Codex does the part only a reader can: deciding what the parts of your app *are*, and saying so plainly. Details in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md).\n\n**Languages:** TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Scala, plus Vue, Svelte and Astro files, with lighter support for others.<br>\n**Endpoints:** Express, Koa, Hono, Next.js, Firebase Cloud Functions, Flask, FastAPI, Django, Go's net/http, Gin, Echo and chi, Actix, Axum, Spring.<br>\n**Screens:** Next.js, React Router, Vue, SvelteKit, Remix, Nuxt, Astro, Expo, Angular, TanStack.\n\n## What it adds to your project\n\nA `floorplan/` folder holding the map. In Claude Code it also adds a short section to `CLAUDE.local.md` so future sessions know the map is there. **Neither is committed:** the folder ignores itself in git, and `CLAUDE.local.md` goes in your clone's private ignore list. In Codex, only the `floorplan/` folder is added. Your `.gitignore` and other tracked files are never touched. See [What's in your project](docs/project-files.md).\n\n## Privacy\n\n- The scan, the map and its small local server all run on your computer. The server only accepts connections from your own machine.\n- No dependencies or install scripts, and the map works offline: its layout engine and fonts are built in.\n- Questions on the map go to your own account, through the Claude Code CLI or Codex, which can read your code but not change it.\n- The Health check never stores or shows secret values, only where they are.\n- No analytics or tracking. The map may ask once whether you'd like an email when Floorplan Cloud launches. Nothing is sent unless you sign up, and then only your email and \"just me\" or \"with my team\".\n\nMore in [Privacy and security](docs/privacy-and-security.md).\n\n## Documentation\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md) | Install, first map, updating, planning from a PRD, removing |\n| [Floorplan in Codex](docs/codex.md) | Installing and using it in Codex |\n| [Using the map](docs/using-the-map.md) | Every button, view, shortcut and menu |\n| [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md) | The pipeline, connection matching, refreshes |\n| [What's in your project](docs/project-files.md) | Every file Floorplan creates, and how to edit it |\n| [Privacy and security](docs/privacy-and-security.md) | What runs where, and what leaves your machine |\n| [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Common problems and fixes |\n| [Developing Floorplan](docs/development.md) | Repo layout, local installs, releases |\n\n## FAQ\n\n<details>\n<summary><b>Does my code leave my computer?</b></summary>\n\nOnly the way Claude Code and Codex always work: the AI reads the files it needs to describe your app, through your own account. The map itself is a local file and its server only listens on your machine. If you choose to open the map in the Claude app instead, Claude uploads the map (names, descriptions and structure, not your source code) to your private claude.ai account, and asks first. The one thing Floorplan itself ever sends is your email, and only if you sign up for the [Floorplan Cloud waitlist](docs/privacy-and-security.md#floorplan-cloud-waitlist).\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><b>How long does it take, and what does it cost?</b></summary>\n\nA first map takes a few minutes for a small app and longer for a big one, because every file and endpoint gets described. It uses your Claude or ChatGPT plan like any other task. Big projects are split across parallel helpers. Updates re-read only what changed, so they're quick and cheap.\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><b>Do I need a CLI for the Ask bar?</b></summary>\n\nNo. The map works without one. The Ask bar answers through the Claude Code CLI or Codex, which can read your real code. Codex's desktop app already includes what it needs. With... (truncated)

Two of them address exactly the problems we've been working through.

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Floorplan haydenschmitty codebase interactive architecture visualization GitHub project screenshot" aspectRatio="4:3" maxWidth="132px"/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Link url="https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan" title="Floorplan"/>** — [3:39](https://youtu.be/S8g5nwZN9as?t=219)

      It maps source files, imports, frontend requests, backend routes, and dependencies—even across repositories. It provides a zoomable, plain-English architectural view.

      **Direct application:** turn our source inventory into a navigable explanation of how the components actually connect, including relationships that the first graph hasn't traced yet.
    </box>

  <divider color="subtle"/>

    <AsyncImage query="Kinetograph 0xS4N4TG programmatic video engine studio timeline Rust compositor screenshot" aspectRatio="4:3" maxWidth="132px"/>

      A programmable video engine combining TypeScript, animation, graphics, audio, Rust GPU compositing, and FFmpeg encoding.

      **Direct application:** a potential route from Nerd Court's scripted scenes and shot instructions to actual encoded video, instead of stopping at SpriteKit playback.
    </box>
  </row>

Kinetograph's own documentation labels it **beta (v0.2.5)**, so its impressive demonstration render times aren't yet evidence that it can produce our full courtroom episodes. But it is a concrete engine worth testing, rather than another hypothetical rendering architecture.

## Two licensing and deployment catches

The upstream repositories revealed constraints the video doesn't explain:

- **<Link url="https://github.com/Pika-Labs/Pika-H3-Flex" title="Pika H3 Flex"/>** ([7:52](https://youtu.be/S8g5nwZN9as?t=472)) can generate reference-guided video with synchronized audio, but the published model license excludes the United States, EU, UK, and South Korea. Its Apache-2.0 code license is separate from the model license. It belongs in the experimental shortlist, **not an approved production dependency** without appropriate licensing. The hosted API would require a separate terms review.
- **Kinetograph** uses the **PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0** license rather than a conventional unrestricted open-source license. That's potentially workable, but its business-size, revenue, and redistribution conditions need reviewing before adoption.

Floorplan has another useful distinction: its generated map normally stays local and uncommitted. That makes it a possible **interactive inspection layer on top of our versioned graph**, not a replacement for the source-backed graph stored in GitHub.

Additional GPUs can run independent requests; this package does not shard one request across GPUs.\n\n## Tested requests\n\nThe following representative cases passed on H100 80GB. Coverage does not establish support for every input combination or maximum reference count.\n\n| Task | Resolution | Requested duration | Memory mode |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Text generation | 480p | 5 / 15 seconds | Default |\n| First, last, or both endpoint frames | 480p | 5 seconds | Default |\n| Text, image, or both endpoint frames | 768p | 5 seconds | Default |\n| Image references | 480p / 768p | 5 seconds | Default |\n| Image + video + audio references | 480p | 5 seconds | Default |\n| Text or image references | 768p | 15 seconds | CPU offload |\n\nSquare and portrait text generation have also passed representative checks. Encoded outputs are checked against the packaged aspect-ratio buckets, expected frame counts, 24 fps and 32 kHz stereo audio. H200 and B300 have not been qualified for this package.\n\n## Memory and performance\n\nDefault 480p/5s sampling allocated approximately 66–69 GiB in representative tests. Default 768p/15s exceeded H100 memory; use `--cpu-offload` for that shape.\n\nCPU offload streams transformer blocks from pinned host memory. Representative 768p/15s sampling allocated approximately 29–32 GiB on GPU, with observed host memory near 94 GiB including page cache. Leave additional headroom for references, longer prompts, dependencies and output buffers. These measurements are not minimum system requirements. The text encoder and VAEs have separate memory requirements, and sampling allocation excludes those stages.\n\nAllow at least 211 GB for base components plus approximately 5.5 GB for both adapters, with additional space for dependencies and download staging. Python 3.12, a supported NVIDIA driver, and the pinned package dependencies are required.\n\nPip, Conda and Docker installation paths have been exercised. Generation is not guaranteed to be bit-exact across kernels, devices, processes or offload modes. Local base/conditioner overrides are trusted inputs and their full shard inventories are not rehashed by the CLI.",

[L2]   "content": "---\ntitle: Use with agents\ndescription: Give a coding agent the Kinetograph skill and MCP tools so it can write, check and render videos.\n---\n\nAn agent can't watch a video, so Kinetograph gives it two things instead. A skill teaches it a loop: write, look, check, render. The agent can write a Remotion-shaped TSX project or an HTML page (HyperFrames projects render as they are); the loop is the same. An MCP server lets it run each CLI command as a tool and see frames as images.\n\n## What an agent gets\n\n**The skill** is a folder with a `SKILL.md` that the agent reads. It covers the loop below, how a project is laid out (`registerRoot`, `Composition`, the native elements and effects), sound, Remotion compatibility and `doctor`, and the CLI flags an agent needs.\n\n**The MCP server** is `npx kinetograph mcp`, over stdio. It has one tool for each CLI command except `studio`, which keeps running until stopped. A tool takes the same arguments as its command. Command names with a space use an underscore. An error comes back as `{ \"error\": { \"code\", \"message\" } }`.\n\n| Tool | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `compositions` | List the compositions of a project |\n| `still` | Render one frame to a PNG; returns the image |\n| `strip` | Contact sheet of evenly spaced frames, labelled with frame and time; returns the image |\n| `onion` | Frames of a range blended over one another, to show a motion path; returns the image |\n| `inspect` | The scene graph at a frame: layers, bounds and resolved styles |\n| `lint` | Text overflowing its box or the canvas, layers off the canvas, overlapping text, missing fonts and assets, type errors, and what the engine can't draw from a Remotion project |\n| `check` | Type errors in the project (`tsc --noEmit`), such as a misspelled prop that renders without an error |\n| `doctor` | What a project holds that the engine cannot draw, and in which frames; with no entry, what this install can do |\n| `render` | Render frames to a video with audio |\n| `snapshot` | Compare frames with the approved PNGs in `__snapshots__/` next to the entry |\n| `audio_analyze` | Loudness (LUFS), true peak, clipping and silences of the mixed audio |\n| `bench` | Milliseconds per frame for each stage |\n| `effects` | List the effects and their parameters |\n\nFor `still`, `strip` and `onion`, `output` is optional: the server writes a temporary PNG and returns it. `render` needs `output`.\n\n## Set up the MCP server\n\nEvery client below runs the same command, `npx -y kinetograph mcp`. You need Node 22 or newer. A GPU is used when there is one, otherwise the CPU.\n\n### Claude Code\n\n```bash\nclaude mcp add kinetograph -- npx -y kinetograph mcp\n```\n\nThis saves the server for the current project. Add `--scope project` to write it to `.mcp.json` for the team, or `--scope user` to use it in every project.\n\n### Claude Desktop\n\nOpen Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config. The file is `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS and `%APPDATA%\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"kinetograph\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"kinetograph\", \"mcp\"]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nQuit and restart Claude Desktop after saving.\n\n### Cursor\n\nPut this in `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"kinetograph\": {\n      \"type\": \"stdio\",\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"-y\", \"kinetograph\", \"mcp\"]\n    }",

A DOM island is handed to Rust, styled by Stylo, laid out by taffy and Parley through\nBlitz's DOM (`blitz-dom` 0.3.0-beta.3, which uses the same Parley 0.12 and taffy 0.15 as the core), and painted by our\nown compositor. Blitz's painter (`blitz-paint`) is not used. No Chrome in the render path, ever; Chrome for Testing is used only by tests and tools to make reference\nimages.\n\nSuccess, measured on the M4:\n- The tiny-agent episode 13 papercut project (`$KINETOGRAPH_CORPUS/tiny-agent/episodes/13-mods/papercut/src/index.ts`,\n  `ModsPapercut`, 988 frames) renders with every frame native.\n- Each frame looks like Chrome's: the golden cases and `scripts/corpus.mjs --reference` against Chrome and Remotion references within a per-pixel threshold (text and\n  anti-aliasing differ; byte equality is not the goal).\n- `cargo test`, clippy, fmt and every npm suite pass; `bench` does not regress.\n\n## 1. Pipeline\n\n```\nReact tree (DOM host elements + native kg-* ones)\n  emit (packages/react/src/emit.ts), per frame: each outermost run of DOM nodes is an island\n    TS (runtime): DomNode tree → IslandRequest JSON: tags, attributes, style as CSS text, stylesheets, time\n    addon renderDomIsland(json)  (crates/node/src/dom.rs)\n      Rust (document): IslandRequest → blitz_dom::BaseDocument; fonts, images; resolve(time): Stylo + layout\n      Rust (paint): paint(doc) → scene layers in CSS paint order; core gains what boxes need\n      Rust (svg): <svg> subtrees and filter graphs → scene layers and a filterGraph effect\n    → IslandOutput JSON: layers, unsupported, camera\n  frame loop, render: every frame is drawn by the addon; unsupported items are warned about, `--strict` fails (the Remotion compatibility docs, `/docs/compat/`)\n```\n\nReadback (`getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetWidth`, `getComputedStyle`, `ResizeObserver`) goes through the same\ndocument: `domLayoutBoxes(json)` in the addon answers for the island's current host tree; the TS DOM shim\ncalls it lazily and caches by tree generation.\n\n## 2. The contract\n\n`crates/dom/src/request.rs` is the contract. In short:\n\n- `IslandRequest { root: DomNode, stylesheets, viewport, fonts, baseDir, publicDir?, time, path, history? }` (`history`: earlier tree states, for CSS transitions, §7.12).\n- `DomNode` = `element { tag, path, attrs, style, children }` | `text { text }` | `native { path, width?, height? }`.\n  `style` is CSS declaration text (`width: 10px; opacity: 0.5`), serialized by TS with React's rules.\n- `IslandOutput { layers: LayerJson[], unsupported: Unsupported[], camera }`, the shape of `IslandResult`.\n  A `{\"type\": \"native\", \"path\", \"x\", \"y\", \"width\", \"height\"}` layer marks where a native element's layers go.\n- Layer ids: derived from the node's explicit `id` attribute if it is a valid layer id, else its `path`, with the\n  suffixes the painter needs (`.bg`, `.border`, `.text`, …), unique per island.\n- Addon functions: `renderDomIsland(requestJson: string, pass?: number): string` and\n  `domLayoutBoxes(requestJson: string): string` → `{ [path]: { x, y, width, height, rect: {x,y,width,height},\n  client: {width,height}, scroll: {width,height} } }` (offset box in island coordinates; `rect` is the transformed\n  bounding box, as `getBoundingClientRect` gives).\n- `pass` numbers the renders of one frame (its own and its motion-blur sub-frames'; compat's `beginSamplePass`). Rules:\n\n- **Paths.** An element's `path` is its place in the host tree: its index among the elements of its parent (DOM and\n  `kg-*` alike, text counts for nothing, a `<Sequence>` is transparent), under the parent's path; top-level ones are\n  `$0`, `$1`. Native elements inside an island count in the numbering, so the paths of Rust's answer and of TypeScript\n  agree.\n- **Attributes** follow React DOM: `className` is `class`, `htmlFor` is `for`, SVG presentation props are hyphenated\n  (`strokeWidth` is `stroke-width`, `clipPath` is `clip-path`, `xlinkHref` is `xlink:href`) while SVG's camelCase\n  attributes keep their case (`viewBox`, `gradientUnits`, `stdDeviation`); HTML names are lower-cased; `true` is `\"\"`\n  for boolean attributes, `false` leaves them out; handlers, `ref`, `key` and `children` are not attributes.\n- **`style`** is CSS declaration text by React's rules: numbers get `px` except `0`, custom properties and the unitless\n  properties (`opacity`, `zIndex`, `flexGrow`, `lineHeight`, `fontWeight`, `scale`, `order`, `aspectRatio`,\n  `strokeWidth`, … and their `Webkit`/`Moz`/`ms`/`O` prefixed forms); camelCase becomes kebab-case, `WebkitX` becomes\n  `-webkit-x`, `msX` `-ms-x`, `cssFloat` `float`; null, booleans and `''` leave the declaration out.\n- **`<style>`, `<link rel=stylesheet href>` and `.css` imports** are the document's stylesheets, the same for every\n  island of the tree (a `<style>` in one island applies in another, as in one document), in this order: imports (in\n  import order), then every `<style>` element and local `<link>` in tree order. Each package builds `src/` to `dist/` with `tsc`\nand tests `test/` with vitest 5 (`*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`); the addon's CPU tests are `node --test`. Workspace packages import each other by package name (resolved through `dist/`), so build\nbefore testing. Relative imports carry `.js` extensions (`moduleResolution: NodeNext`).\n\n| Path | Package | What |\n|---|---|---|\n| `crates/node` | `@kinetographdev/native` | napi-rs addon over `kinetograph-core` and the `kinetograph-cli` encoder (§3) |\n| `crates/core`, `crates/cli` | Rust | scene features, renderer reuse, `inspect.rs`, the encoder (§4) |\n| `packages/scene` | `@kinetographdev/scene` | TS types of the whole SCENE.md schema, effect and paint helpers, motion-blur JSON helpers (§5) |\n| `packages/react` | `@kinetographdev/react` | `react-reconciler` host config, native elements, `TimelineContext` (§6) |\n| `packages/core` | `@kinetographdev/core` | Remotion core API, frame loop, determinism shim, the pure-TS Remotion packages as subpaths (§7) |\n| `packages/audio` | `@kinetographdev/audio` | `onFrame`, offline mix through `node-web-audio-api`, loudness analysis (§8) |\n| `packages/cli` | `kinetograph` (bin `kinetograph`) | the CLI commands, the MCP server, project bundling (§9) |\n\nDependencies point one way: `scene` ← `react` ← `core`; `cli` uses `core`, `audio`, `native`; `core` uses `native` only\nfor text measurement (`layout-utils`). `react` and `react-reconciler` are peer dependencies of `@kinetographdev/react` and\n`@kinetographdev/core`, so a project has one React.\n\nThese determinism rules hold everywhere: rendering is a pure function of (project, frame); nothing\nreads the wall clock (benchmarks aside) or calls an unseeded random generator; fonts are registered before any text is\nmeasured; Remotion APIs are written from Remotion's documentation, never from its source.\n\n## 2. Keyframe lists remain legal in it.\n\n## 3. `@kinetographdev/native`\n\n`crates/node`, built with `@napi-rs/cli` (`npm run build` debug, `npm run build:release` for benchmarks). `napi build`\ngenerates the loader `index.js` and `index.d.ts` from `src/lib.rs`; both are committed. [L2]   "content": "# Unified Nerd Court — architecture proposal v0.1\n\n**Status: proposal, not implemented.** This design reflects the source-backed graph and user product requirements recorded October 28, 2026.\n\n## Plain-English system behavior\n\n1. A viewer types a grievance and optional character names.\n2. UATU identifies whether names refer to a fictional character, continuity-specific version, actor, role portrayed by an actor, or a real/historical person.\n3. It finds the appropriate source evidence, distinguishes credible canon from interpretation, and asks for clarification only when essential to avoid a different individual.\n4. UATU uses cross-portrayal archetype *gestalt* as background while compiling **separate, continuity-bounded variant profiles**. It creates temporary performance echoes, voice and visual briefs and a **versioned CastManifest**.\n5. Nerd Court receives the evidence and cast, conducts structured prosecution/defense, performs character-specific dialogue and witnesses, produces a cited verdict and permits an earned comedic or dramatic finisher.\n6. A production pipeline storyboards, records/synthesizes approved voices, animates shots, mixes, renders, encodes and checks a real video master.\n7. Job services keep the viewer informed, manage costs, persist published assets and optionally preserve an exact echo snapshot for a sequel. The video is playable via browser, phone or television app.\n\n## Proposed single-repo layout\n\n```text\nnerd-court/\n  architecture/knowledge-graph/      # current source-backed architecture records\n  architecture/contracts/            # versioned JSON interfaces (first migration unit)\n  apps/\n    web/                             # grievance, jobs, episode archive, player [PLANNED]\n    tv/                              # streaming-platform client [PLANNED]\n    ios-legacy/                      # move existing Swift code only after audit [PLANNED]\n  services/\n    identity/                        # classify and resolve actor / portrayal / variant [PLANNED]\n    canon-evidence/                  # claim provenance, tiered canon, conflicts [PLANNED]\n    uatu-casting/                    # variant psychology, ephemeral echoes, cast [PLANNED]\n    courtroom/                       # adversarial trial, judge and finisher rules [PLANNED]\n    showrunner/                       # scenes, timing, boards [PLANNED]\n    media-render/                     # animation, sound, encoding, QC [PLANNED]\n    jobs/                            # retries, idempotency, visibility [PLANNED]\n  packages/\n    contracts/                       # generated language bindings after schema review [PLANNED]\n    shared-tests/                     # source-backed fixtures, no cross-variant leakage [PLANNED]\n  infra/                              # deploy, access, secrets and storage policy [PLANNED]\n  docs/                               # operational how-to and design decisions [PLANNED]\n  Sources/, Tests/, convex/           # EXISTING Swift/Convex code, untouched on feature branch\n```\n\nThe layout is **a target**, not a claim that these directories or components exist today. Do not migrate by mass-copying the old repos; use pinned-source references until a candidate module has a passing characterization test and known license.\n\n## Identity contract\n\nThe identity hierarchy is `Archetype -> Variant -> EpisodeEcho`, with **parallel** entity types for performers and portrayals:\n\n- **Archetype:** an evidence-aware gestalt across portrayals; may contain conflicting versions, explicitly tagged.\n- **Variant:** fixed franchise, publisher, medium, universe, timeline, role, and era; exact source claims and relationship bounds.\n- **Performer:** real actor/person, not equivalent to an authored character; `portrays` is a typed edge, not an `is` edge.\n- **Portrayal:** an actor playing a role *in a named production* and, if applicable, within a specified fictional world.\n- **EpisodeEcho:** temporary performance state pinned to one variant or portrayal, one episode and one profile revision. The underlying canon never mutates when fiction happens in court.\n\nAs an example, **Robert Downey Jr., MCU Tony Stark, Downey's Lewis Strauss portrayal, Downey's Charlie Chaplin portrayal, and a specifically chosen Doctor Doom portrayal are five distinct records** even if jokes intentionally connect them. Do not assume Doom is MCU Stark in disguise just because the performer overlaps.\n\n## Data contracts to implement first\n\n- `Grievance`: the allegation, named entities, user constraints, user-entered continuity hints and submission identifier.\n- `EntityResolution`: entity kind, canonical ID, portrayal/actor mapping, evidence and ambiguity score.\n- `VariantProfile`: locked variant keys, citations, observed traits, modeled psychology and inferred claims clearly separated.\n- `CastManifest`: fixed episode ID, source/profile/voice/visual versions, roles, character-echo references, witnesses and provenance.\n- `EvidenceLedger`: citation anchors, direct source material, strength and contradiction handling.\n- `EpisodeJob`: explicit state transitions, inputs/outputs, failure, retries, cost, timing, artifact verification.\n- `EpisodeArtifact`: decodable video renditions, synchronized audio, captions, media hashes, review status and publication URI.\n\n## Boundaries that must not collapse\n\n| Boundary | Contract |\n|---|---|\n| Archetype vs variant | Gesture toward archetype for interpretation; do not import unrelated history or speech |\n| Variant vs performer | Link with `portrays`; never unify identities |\n| Research vs performance | Fact selection and uncertainty completed before actors begin improvising |\n| Episode improvisation vs source canon | Show-only events are in episode history, not canonical evidence |\n| Runtime echo vs durable profile | Echo lives for a job; serialize only if reuse approved |\n| Psychological inference vs observable canon | Mark estimates/hypotheses separately from cited actions |\n| Sound/animation playback vs video file | A scene executing in SpriteKit is not proof of encoded streaming media |\n| Completion flag vs acceptance | `SUCCESS` requires verified playable A/V output, not just a scripted transcript |\n\n## Build order\n\n**Phase A (current):** pin repos, construct knowledge graph and an explicit source/destination ledger, identify licensing and security exclusions.  \n**Phase B:** define versioned contracts; implement and test classification, continuity resolution and source ledger on a curated cross-franchise fixture set.  \n**Phase C:** integrate UATU deep assessment and a variant-exclusive compiler; test identity drift and echo lifecycle under restarts and crossover stimuli.  \n**Phase D:** integrate court debate, an evidence-backed judge, scene plans, staff/guest roles and finisher choreography; validate a complete **text-and-shot-plan trial**.  \n**Phase E:** implement actual animation, voice approvals, mixing, render/encode, captions and media validation; prove one complete A/V episode before scaling.  \n**Phase F:** add web + TV distribution, durable jobs, budgets, caching, observability, live capacity and measured long-episode turnaround.\n\nEach phase has its own acceptance tests; no phase is declared complete merely because a file or API route exists.\n\n## Graph-first development rule\n\nWhen a new module is merged:\n1. Add its source/provenance and destination owner node.\n2. Add observed import/call/data-flow edges after reviewing the actual code.\n3. Add a corresponding executable test and runtime status.\n4. Resolve discrepancies between aspirational README claims and implementation evidence.\n5. Maintain pinning and ensure no secret, licensed binary, or unwanted memory scope travels between repos.\n",

    def test_all_shapes_receive_individual_clipped_print_screens(self):
        svg = render_svg(BASE)
        root = ElementTree.fromstring(svg)
        ns = "{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}"
        patterns = root.findall(".//" + ns + "pattern")

        self.assertIn('fill="url(#dots-test-actor)"', svg)
        self.assertNotIn('dots-caption', svg)

    def test_dot_radius_stays_constant_when_dot_density_changes(self):
        svg = render_svg(BASE)
        ns = "{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}"
        pats = ElementTree.fromstring(svg).findall(".//" + ns + "pattern")
        self.assertNotEqual(pats[0].attrib["width"], pats[1].attrib["width"])
        self.assertEqual(pats[0].find(ns + "circle").attrib["r"],
                         pats[1].find(ns + "circle").attrib["r"])

    def test_dots_cover_shapes_even_when_density_is_omitted(self):
        scene = {"width": 200, "height": 100,
                 "layers": [{"id": "wall", "type": "rect", "x": 0, "y": 0,
                             "width": 200, "height": 100, "fill": "violet"}]}
        self.assertIn('id="dots-wall"', render_svg(scene))

    def test_actor_local_screen_moves_with_actor_and_camera_screen_does_not(self):
        scene = {"width": 200, "height": 100, "layers": [
            {"id": "actor", "type": "circle", "cx": 50, "cy": 50, "r": 24,
             "translate": [10, 5], "anchor": "object", "fill": "cyan"},
            {"id": "background", "type": "rect", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 80, "height": 80,
             "translate": [10, 5], "anchor": "screen", "fill": "violet"},
        ]}
        svg = render_svg(scene)
        ns = "{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}"
        pats = ElementTree.fromstring(svg).findall(".//" + ns + "pattern")
        self.assertIn("translate(0 0)", pats[0].attrib["patternTransform"])
        self.assertIn("translate(-10 -5)", pats[1].attrib["patternTransform"])

    def test_identical_inputs_render_to_identical_svg(self):
        self.assertEqual(render_svg(BASE, frame=17), render_svg(BASE, frame=17))

    def test_text_is_escaped_and_remains_undotted(self):
        scene = {"width": 220, "height": 90, "layers": [
            {"id": "caption", "type": "text", "x": 20, "y": 60,
             "text": '"DOOM" <TONY> & co.', "fill": "paper"},
        ]}
        svg = render_svg(scene)
        ElementTree.fromstring(svg)
        self.assertIn('&lt;TONY&gt; &amp; co.', svg)
        self.assertNotIn('<TONY>', svg)
        self.assertNotIn('<pattern', svg)

    def test_rejects_invalid_svg_injection_and_style_values(self):
        cases = [
            {"id": "a", "type": "path", "d": 'M 0 0 L 1 1" onload="evil()"', "fill": "cyan"},
            {"id": "bad space", "type": "rect", "x": 1, "y": 1, "width": 2, "height": 2},
            {"id": "valid", "type": "rect", "x": 1, "y": 1, "width": 2, "height": 2, "fill": "url(http://evil)"},
            {"id": "valid", "type": "circle", "cx": 10, "cy": 10, "r": 4, "dots": "fuzzy"},
        ]
        for entry in cases:
            with self.subTest(entry=entry):
                with self.assertRaises(BenDayError):
                    render_svg({"width": 120, "height": 90, "layers": [entry]})

    def test_rejects_duplicate_ids_invalid_coordinates_and_frame(self):
        sc = {"width": 150, "height": 90, "layers": [
            {"id": "z", "type": "circle", "cx": 10, "cy": 10, "r": 4},
            {"id": "z", "type": "circle", "cx": 30, "cy": 30, "r": 4},
        ]}
        with self.assertRaises(BenDayError):
            render_svg(sc)
        with self.assertRaises(BenDayError):
            render_svg({"width": -1, "height": 90, "layers": []})
        with self.assertRaises(BenDayError):
            render_svg(BASE, frame=-1)

    def test_palette_consistent_for_all_frames(self):
        svg = render_svg(BASE, frame=90)
        for color in (PALETTE["violet"], PALETTE["magenta"], PALETTE["cyan"]):
            self.assertIn(color, svg)
        self.assertEqual(9, len(PALETTE))

    def test_independent_registrations_are_deterministic(self):
        scene = {"width": 200, "height": 120,
                 "registration": [2, -1],
                 "layers": [{"id": "a", "type": "rect", "x": 0, "y": 0,
                             "width": 180, "height": 100, "fill": "cyan"}]}
        svg = render_svg(scene)
        self.assertIn("translate(2 -1)", svg)
        self.assertEqual(svg, render_svg(scene))

    def test_svg_can_rasterize_to_a_real_image(self):
        try:
            import cairosvg
            from PIL import Image
            from io import BytesIO
        except ImportError:
            self.skipTest("Optional raster proof requires cairosvg and Pillow")
        raster = cairosvg.svg2png(bytestring=render_svg(BASE).encode("utf-8"))
        im = Image.open(BytesIO(raster)).convert("RGB")
        self.assertEqual(im.size, (320, 180))
        self.assertNotEqual(im.getpixel((74, 78)), im.getpixel((8, 8)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Deterministic, layer-clipped Ben-Day SVG print stage for Nerd Court.

Ben-Day flat-tint screens contain equal-sized dots; visual density changes by
spacing them, rather than resizing every dot to match pixel luminance. This
module draws material-aware screens, not a disposable whole-frame overlay.

The output is ordinary SVG, which can be rasterized or consumed as a media
asset by a separate video encoder. No Kinetograph/SpriteKit connection is
claimed by this package.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from html import escape
from typing import Any, Mapping


class BenDayError(ValueError):
    """Invalid or unsafe scene specification."""


PALETTE = {
    "paper": "#F5ECDD",
    "graphite": "#17131F",
    "violet": "#34204F",
    "magenta": "#F14693",
    "cyan": "#48D3DF",
    "yellow": "#F5CC50",
    "crimson": "#DB3954",
    "amber": "#C69E5D",
    "slate": "#607A9D",
}

# These screens use the *same physical dot radius* at different pitches.
DOT_SCREENS = {"open": 24.0, "medium": 15.0, "dense": 10.0, "impact": 7.5}
DOT_RADIUS = 2.6
# Channel angles keep overlapped screens from all landing on one grid.
INK_ANGLES = {"cyan": 15, "magenta": 75, "yellow": 0, "graphite": 45,
              "crimson": 45, "amber": 0, "slate": 15, "violet": 75, "paper": 0}
_ID = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$")
_HEX = re.compile(r"^#[a-fA-F0-9]{6}$")
_SVG_PATH = re.compile(r"^[MmLlHhVvCcSsQqTtAaZz0-9,.\s+\-eE]+$")


def _num(value: Any, field: str, *, positive: bool = False) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        raise BenDayError(f"{field} must be numeric")
    try:
        v = float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:
        raise BenDayError(f"{field} must be numeric") from exc
    if not math.isfinite(v) or abs(v) > 10000 or (positive and v <= 0):
        raise BenDayError(f"{field} outside permitted range")
    return f"{v:g}"


def _color(value: Any) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, str) and value in PALETTE:
        return PALETTE[value]
    if isinstance(value, str) and _HEX.fullmatch(value):
        return value.upper()
    raise BenDayError("Color must be a palette name or six-digit hex value")


def _pair(value: Any, name: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    if not isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) or len(value) != 2:
        raise BenDayError(f"{name} must be a two-number array")
    return float(_num(value[0], name)), float(_num(value[1], name))


def _shape(layer: Mapping[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return safe SVG shape tag plus sanitized geometric attributes."""
    kind = layer["type"]
    attrs: dict[str, str]
    if kind == "rect":
        attrs = {k: _num(layer.get(k), k, positive=k in ("width", "height"))
                 for k in ("x", "y", "width", "height")}
    elif kind == "circle":
        attrs = {k: _num(layer.get(k), k, positive=k == "r")
                 for k in ("cx", "cy", "r")}
    elif kind == "ellipse":
        attrs = {k: _num(layer.get(k), k, positive=k in ("rx", "ry"))
                 for k in ("cx", "cy", "rx", "ry")}
    elif kind == "path":
        d = layer.get("d")
        if not isinstance(d, str) or not d or len(d) > 12000 or not _SVG_PATH.fullmatch(d):
            raise BenDayError("Invalid SVG path data")
        attrs = {"d": d}
    elif kind == "polygon":
        points = layer.get("points")
        if not isinstance(points, list) or len(points) < 3 or len(points) > 500:
            raise BenDayError("polygon requires 3–500 vertices")
        coords = [_pair(p, "polygon point") for p in points]
        attrs = {"points": " ".join(f"{x:g},{y:g}" for x, y in coords)}
    else:
        raise BenDayError(f"Unsupported painted shape type: {kind!r}")
    return kind, " ".join(f'{k}="{escape(v, quote=True)}"' for k, v in attrs.items())


def render_svg(scene: Mapping[str, Any], *, frame: int = 0) -> str:
    """Render one fully specified frame as a deterministic Ben-Day SVG.

    scene: {width,height,layers:[shape|text], registration:[x,y]}
    Shapes are solid flat inks with their own uniform-dot tint screens;
    labels/text are rendered *after* printed surfaces and never dithered.

    The caller controls geometry, color choices, camera translation, and
    character poses. Dots default to 'medium', not 'none', for every shape.
    Dots are object-locked by default, screen-locked when anchor='screen'.
    """
    if not isinstance(scene, Mapping):
        raise BenDayError("scene must be a mapping")
    if isinstance(frame, bool) or not isinstance(frame, int) or frame < 0 or frame > 10**8:
        raise BenDayError("frame must be a nonnegative integer")
    width = _num(scene.get("width"), "width", positive=True)
    height = _num(scene.get("height"), "height", positive=True)
    layers = scene.get("layers")
    if not isinstance(layers, list) or len(layers) > 512:
        raise BenDayError("layers must be an array of at most 512 objects")
    register_x, register_y = _pair(scene.get("registration", [0, 0]), "registration")
    paper = _color(scene.get("paper", "paper"))
    defs: list[str] = []
    art: list[str] = []
    text_art: list[str] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()

    for layer in layers:
        if not isinstance(layer, Mapping):
            raise BenDayError("each layer must be an object")
        ident = layer.get("id")
        if not isinstance(ident, str) or not _ID.fullmatch(ident) or ident in seen_ids:
            raise BenDayError("layer id must be unique, short and safe")
        seen_ids.add(ident)
        tx, ty = _pair(layer.get("translate", [0, 0]), "translate")
        trans = f'translate({tx:g} {ty:g})'
        fill = _color(layer.get("fill", "paper"))
        opacity = _num(layer.get("opacity", 1), "opacity")
        if not 0 <= float(opacity) <= 1:
            raise BenDayError("opacity outside [0,1]")
        if layer.get("type") == "text":
            # Captions, nameplates, verdicts and subtitles never receive dot masks.
            x, y = (_num(layer.get(k), k) for k in ("x", "y"))
            size = _num(layer.get("font_size", 20), "font_size", positive=True)
            weight = "700" if layer.get("bold", True) else "400"
            if not isinstance(layer.get("text"), str) or len(layer["text"]) > 1500:
                raise BenDayError("text must be a string of at most 1500 characters")
            text_art.append(f'<g transform="{trans}" opacity="{opacity}"><text id="{ident}" '
                            f'x="{x}" y="{y}" fill="{fill}" font-size="{size}" '
                            f'font-family="DejaVu Sans, sans-serif" font-weight="{weight}">'
                            f'{escape(layer["text"])}</text></g>')
            continue

        tag, geom = _shape(layer)
        dots = layer.get("dots", "medium")
        if dots not in (*DOT_SCREENS.keys(), "none"):
            raise BenDayError("unknown Ben-Day dot screen")
        ink = _color(layer.get("stroke", "graphite"))
        outline = _num(layer.get("stroke_width", 2.5), "stroke_width")
        if float(outline) < 0:
            raise BenDayError("stroke_width must not be negative")
        body = [f'<{tag} {geom} fill="{fill}"/>']
        if dots != "none":
            dot_color_name = layer.get("dot_color", "graphite")
            dot_color = _color(dot_color_name)
            angle = INK_ANGLES.get(dot_color_name, 45)
            pitch = DOT_SCREENS[dots]
            if pitch <= 2 * DOT_RADIUS:
                raise BenDayError("dot screen spacing too small for radius")
            anchor = layer.get("anchor", "object")
            if anchor not in ("object", "screen"):
                raise BenDayError("anchor must be 'object' or 'screen'")
            shift_x = register_x - (tx if anchor == "screen" else 0)
            shift_y = register_y - (ty if anchor == "screen" else 0)
            pid = f"dots-{ident}"
            defs.append(f'<pattern id="{pid}" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" '
                        f'width="{pitch:g}" height="{pitch:g}" '
                        f'patternTransform="translate({shift_x:g} {shift_y:g}) rotate({angle})">'
                        f'<circle cx="{pitch/2:g}" cy="{pitch/2:g}" r="{DOT_RADIUS:g}" '
                        f'fill="{dot_color}"/></pattern>')
            body.append(f'<{tag} {geom} fill="url(#{pid})"/>')
        if float(outline) > 0:
            body.append(f'<{tag} {geom} fill="none" stroke="{ink}" '
                        f'stroke-width="{outline}" stroke-linejoin="round"/>')
        art.append(f'<g id="{ident}" transform="{trans}" opacity="{opacity}">'
                   + "".join(body) + "</g>")

    return (f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" '
            f'viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" data-frame="{frame}">'
            f'<defs>{"".join(defs)}</defs><rect width="{width}" height="{height}" '
            f'fill="{paper}"/>{"".join(art)}{"".join(text_art)}</svg>')

"""Build an original Ben-Day courtroom style proof as a real H.264/AAC MP4.

This is a renderer smoke test, NOT a Nerd Court episode or UATU integration.
The figures and sounds are original anonymous geometric constructions.
Requires CairoSVG, ffmpeg and ffprobe for local demonstration.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import io
import math
import os
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import tempfile
import wave
from pathlib import Path

from ben_day import render_svg

W, H = 960, 540
FPS = 15
DURATION = 5


def box(id, x, y, width, height, fill, dots="medium", **kw):
    return {"id": id, "type": "rect", "x": x, "y": y, "width": width,
            "height": height, "fill": fill, "dots": dots, **kw}


def poly(id, points, fill, dots="medium", **kw):
    return {"id": id, "type": "polygon", "points": points, "fill": fill, "dots": dots, **kw}


def oval(id, cx, cy, rx, ry, fill, dots="medium", **kw):
    return {"id": id, "type": "ellipse", "cx": cx, "cy": cy, "rx": rx, "ry": ry,
            "fill": fill, "dots": dots, **kw}


def label(id, x, y, text, size=24, fill="paper", **kw):
    return {"id": id, "type": "text", "x": x, "y": y, "text": text,
            "font_size": size, "fill": fill, **kw}


def frame_scene(frame: int, fps: int = FPS) -> dict:
    t = frame / fps
    impact = 3.2 <= t < 4.25
    flick = -3 if impact and frame % 2 == 0 else 3 if impact else 0
    left_shift = -24 * max(0, 1 - t / 0.8)
    right_shift = 24 * max(0, 1 - t / 0.8)
    pitch_shift = -4 if impact and frame % 3 == 0 else 0
    s = {"width": W, "height": H, "registration": [pitch_shift, 0], "layers": []}
    a = s["layers"]
    # Printed graphic novel staging: every architectural surface gets a tint screen.
    a.extend([
        box("stage-wall", 0, 0, W, H, "graphite", "dense", dot_color="slate", stroke_width=0),

    ])
